financials_interim.notes: Same source as GROUP row (source_id 52472), COMPANY STATEMENT OF PROFIT OR LOSS (doc p.7), COMPANY STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL POSITION (doc p.9), COMPANY STATEMENT OF CASH FLOWS (doc p.11) -- LPL's standalone parent, which holds Investments in Subsidiaries of 2,847,068,563 (up from 2,367,068,563 at 31 Mar 2026, a Rs480Mn increase this quarter -- new capital pushed into a subsidiary) rather than consolidating them. See GROUP row's notes for the nil-FX confirmation, the segmental Hydro/Solar analysis (not separately available at Company level, which does not own plant directly), and the hydrology-disclosure gap. Revenue fell 41% (11,470,886 vs 19,584,625 PY) -- the parent's own revenue is a small residual (largely management/other charges to subsidiaries) and is not representative of Group generation revenue. Administrative Expenses fell 68% (8,510,419 vs 26,764,746 PY, a Rs18.25Mn reduction) -- this cost cut narrowed the operating loss by more than half: Operating Loss (6,774,816) vs (16,343,729) PY (-59%, i.e. the loss shrank). However Finance Cost rose 37% (38,287,082 vs 28,048,285 PY, a Rs10.24Mn increase) -- per the Cash Flow statement (doc p.11) this is traced to 'Inter Company Interest Expenses' of 35,276,025 vs 25,567,888 PY (+38%), i.e. rising intercompany interest on loans (likely funding the Rs480Mn subsidiary investment made this quarter, see above) is THE specific driver of the Company-level loss widening, swamping the Admin-cost improvement: Profit/(Loss) Before Tax (34,861,332) vs (30,352,343) PY (+15% wider loss). Income Tax Expense (a credit both periods, per the Company P&L's positive-sign convention) fell 37% (1,448,659 vs 2,316,241 PY), a smaller offsetting benefit, so the bottom-line loss widened 19%: (33,412,673) vs (28,036,102) PY. EPS (0.09) vs (0.07) PY. Foreign Currency Exchange Gain/(Loss) again explicit and nil both periods (doc p.7). Stored tax_expense=-1,448,659 (negative = credit, per profit_before_tax - tax_expense = profit_after_tax convention; matches the raw disclosed positive figure directly, since -34,861,332-(-33,412,673)=-1,448,659). Balance sheet (doc p.9): Trade and Other Payables of 1,566,219,195 is unusually large relative to Company revenue (11,470,886/quarter) -- almost certainly dominated by intercompany/related-party payables given the small standalone revenue base and large Investments in Subsidiaries; flagged since the filing does not break out an intercompany-vs-external split. short_term_borrowings=18,507,697 (16,743,714 current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings + 1,763,983 Bank Overdraft); long_term_borrowings=58,106,511. trade_receivables=607,601,308, trade_payables=1,566,219,195 (combined lines, same flag as GROUP; inventory is nil/not disclosed at Company level, unlike the small 171,012 at Group level). Cash flow (doc p.11): cash_from_operations=42,709,724; capex=(165,147); cash_from_investing=(165,147); cash_from_financing=(5,399,298), driven by a 5,449,069 repayment of interest-bearing loans and borrowings with no offsetting new proceeds this quarter (contrast the Group's large gross CP-style borrowing activity) -- consistent with the subsidiary-investment funding being routed through intercompany loans/interest (the Cash Flow 'Investments in Subsidiaries' outflow itself is not shown as a separate CF line at Company level, only the 480Mn BS movement, since the report's Company CF investing section shows only a small 165,147 PP&E acquisition -- flagged as a gap: the Rs480Mn subsidiary-investment increase visible on the BS is not reconciled to a corresponding CF investing outflow in this statement, likely a non-cash/in-kind or intercompany-loan-funded transaction not separately disclosed). depreciation_amortization=7,376,123 (6,061,275 Depreciation of PP&E + 1,314,848 Amortization of Right-to-use Assets, per CF statement).

Source: LAUGFS Power PLC interim FS for the quarter ended 30 Jun 2026 (unaudited, authorised for issue by the board 13 Aug 2026, subject to audit). Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss doc p.2, Consolidated Statement of Financial Position doc p.5, Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows doc p.6, Operating Segments doc p.12, Notes to the Financial Statements doc p.13-16. Subsidiaries per Corporate Information (doc p.17): Anorchi Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, Ginigathhena Thiniyagala Mini Hydro Power (Pvt) Ltd, Iris Eco Power Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, Pams Power (Pvt) Ltd; parent enterprise LAUGFS Holdings Limited. First-ever financial_statements entry for LPL. Figures are in whole Rupees -- unit_scale='1'. Revenue +10% (222,285,587 vs 201,971,130 PY); Cost of Sales +9% (97,044,092 vs 89,154,790); Gross Profit +11% (125,241,495 vs 112,816,340). Administrative Expenses fell 19% (54,536,145 vs 67,180,678, a Rs12.64Mn reduction) -- this cost discipline, layered on top of revenue growth, is the single most important driver of Operating Profit +55% (70,705,350 vs 45,635,662). Foreign Currency Exchange Gain/(Loss) is explicitly disclosed as a separate P&L line (doc p.2) and reads nil ('-') for both the current and prior-year quarter -- confirmed checked per the project's standing instruction to look for FX exposure at power generators; unlike HPWR, LPL discloses the line but it is genuinely zero this quarter, not omitted. SEGMENTAL DRIVER (doc p.12, Hydro Power vs Solar Power): the PBT swing is driven almost entirely by a dramatic Hydro Power turnaround -- Hydro segment PBT swung from a Rs33,242,489 LOSS (PY) to a Rs16,486,190 PROFIT this quarter (a +Rs49.73Mn swing), on Hydro revenue that more than tripled (43,735,977 vs 12,501,107 PY, +250%) and Hydro operating profit swinging from a Rs16,896,056 loss to a Rs21,508,840 profit. This more than offset a large decline in the Solar Power segment: Solar PBT fell 61.7% (18,841,369 vs 49,144,407 PY), driven by Solar segment Finance Costs surging 55% (80,284,100 vs 51,765,117 PY, a +Rs28.52Mn increase) even as Solar operating profit fell a more modest 21.3% (49,196,510 vs 62,531,718) -- i.e. the Solar segment's PBT decline is a finance-cost story, not an operating one. Net segment math cross-checks exactly against the Group PBT change: Hydro +49,728,679 and Solar -30,303,038 nets to +19,425,641, matching the disclosed Group PBT increase (35,327,559-15,901,918=19,425,641) to the rupee. GAP: the report's Notes (doc p.13, 'Contingencies, capital and other commitments' and 'Events occurring after the reporting date') contain no rainfall/hydrology commentary explaining the Hydro segment's dramatic swing -- inferred purely from the segmental revenue/PBT numbers, not management narrative, and flagged as a genuine disclosure gap (per the project's standing instruction to check for hydrology commentary at hydropower generators). At Group level: Finance Cost +9% (47,461,849 vs 43,364,714) and Finance Income -11% (12,084,058 vs 13,630,970) -- net finance drag actually worsened slightly YoY, so the 122% PBT growth (35,327,559 vs 15,901,918) is attributable to the operating-line improvement (Admin cost cut + Hydro turnaround), not finance items. Income Tax Expense +49% (12,377,515 vs 8,327,582); Profit for the Period +203% (22,950,044 vs 7,574,336). EPS 0.06 vs 0.02 (doc p.2) -- cross-checked: 22,950,044 / 387,000,086 total shares in issue (335,000,086 voting + 52,000,000 non-voting, per Note 5.6, doc p.16) = 0.0593, rounds to 0.06, confirming the EPS denominator includes BOTH voting and non-voting shares; shares_in_issue=387,000,086 used accordingly. Balance sheet (doc p.5, as at 30.06.2026 vs 30.06.2025 vs 31.03.2026 -- a true 3-column comparative unlike MFPE/HPWR): short_term_borrowings=502,227,802 combines current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings (428,696,251) with Bank Overdraft (73,531,551); excludes Lease Liabilities-Short Term (6,357,194), kept separate. long_term_borrowings=1,210,698,874 (non-current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings only; excludes Deferred Tax Liability, Lease Liabilities-Long Term and Retirement Benefit Liability). trade_receivables=1,143,923,484 and trade_payables=191,332,366 are the combined 'Trade and Other Receivables/Payables' lines -- flagged as combined, not pure-trade. Cash flow (doc p.6): cash_from_operations=65,042,497; capex=(40,094,108) ('Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment'); cash_from_investing=(40,094,108); cash_from_financing=114,016,876 -- NOTE: the cash flow statement's own row label reads 'Net Cash Flows USED IN Financing Activities' but the printed value (114,016,876) is POSITIVE, i.e. a net financing INFLOW; verified by reconstructing the line from its components (Finance Income 12,024,194 + Proceeds from Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings 362,565,237 - Repayment of Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings 260,572,555 = 114,016,876, confirming the value, not the label, is correct) -- flagged as a label/printing artifact per the project's standing instruction to guard against extraction artifacts; the positive figure is what is stored. depreciation_amortization=66,175,075 (63,570,052 Depreciation of PP&E + 2,605,023 Amortization of Right-to-use Assets, per CF statement; excludes 2,310,974 'Finance Cost-Right-to-use Assets', which is a finance line not D&A).

interim_updates.note_text: LAUGFS Power PLC (LPL) reported Group Revenue of Rs.222,285,587 for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), +10% YoY (2025: Rs.201,971,130). SEGMENTAL DRIVER (Operating Segments note, doc p.12, Hydro Power vs Solar Power): the PBT growth is driven almost entirely by a dramatic Hydro Power turnaround -- Hydro segment PBT swung from a Rs.33,242,489 LOSS (PY) to a Rs.16,486,190 PROFIT this quarter (a +Rs.49.73mn swing), on Hydro revenue that more than tripled to Rs.43,735,977 (2025: Rs.12,501,107, +250%) and Hydro operating profit swinging from a Rs.16,896,056 loss to a Rs.21,508,840 profit. This more than offset a large decline in the Solar Power segment: Solar PBT fell 61.7% to Rs.18,841,369 (2025: Rs.49,144,407), driven by Solar segment Finance Costs surging 55% to Rs.80,284,100 (2025: Rs.51,765,117, a +Rs.28.52mn increase) even as Solar operating profit fell a more modest 21.3% (Rs.49,196,510 vs Rs.62,531,718) -- the Solar segment's PBT decline is specifically a finance-cost story, not an operating one. Net segment math cross-checks exactly against the Group PBT change: Hydro +Rs.49,728,679 and Solar -Rs.30,303,038 nets to +Rs.19,425,641, matching the disclosed Group PBT increase to the rupee. Administrative Expenses also fell 19% to Rs.54,536,145 (2025: Rs.67,180,678, a Rs.12.64mn reduction), a secondary driver of Operating Profit +55% to Rs.70,705,350 (2025: Rs.45,635,662). Foreign Currency Exchange Gain/(Loss) is explicitly disclosed as a separate P&L line and reads nil for both the current and prior-year quarter -- confirmed checked as genuinely zero this quarter, not omitted (unlike sector peer HPWR, which discloses no FX line at all). Group Finance Cost rose 9% (Rs.47,461,849 vs Rs.43,364,714) and Finance Income fell 11% (Rs.12,084,058 vs Rs.13,630,970) -- net finance drag actually worsened slightly YoY at the Group level, so the 122% PBT growth (Rs.35,327,559 vs Rs.15,901,918) is attributable entirely to the operating-line improvement (Admin cost cut + Hydro turnaround), not to finance items. Income Tax Expense rose 49% to Rs.12,377,515 (2025: Rs.8,327,582); Profit for the Period rose 203% to Rs.22,950,044 (2025: Rs.7,574,336). EPS Rs.0.06 vs Rs.0.02 PY, using a share count of 387,000,086 (335,000,086 voting + 52,000,000 non-voting).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is LPL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no rainfall/hydrology commentary anywhere in the Notes (doc p.13) explains the Hydro segment's dramatic Rs.49.73mn PBT swing or the 250% revenue jump -- the segment driver above is inferred purely from segmental revenue/PBT numbers, not management narrative; (2) at the Company (standalone parent) level, Investments in Subsidiaries rose Rs.480,000,000 this quarter (Rs.2,367,068,563 to Rs.2,847,068,563) but the Company Cash Flow statement's investing section shows only a small Rs.165,147 PP&E acquisition, with no corresponding investing outflow for the Rs.480mn increase -- likely a non-cash or intercompany-loan- funded transaction not separately disclosed, and consistent with Company-level Finance Cost rising 37% on higher 'Inter Company Interest Expenses' (Rs.35,276,025 vs Rs.25,567,888 PY, +38%) which is THE specific driver of the Company-level loss widening to Rs.(33,412,673) from Rs.(28,036,102) PY, even as the Group turned in strong growth; (3) FX exposure is confirmed genuinely nil both periods (unlike sector peer HPWR, which discloses no FX line at all).
interim_updates.takeaway: LPL's 203% PAT growth is driven almost entirely by a Hydro Power segment turnaround -- a Rs.49.73mn PBT swing on revenue more than tripling -- which comfortably offset a Rs.30.30mn PBT decline in the Solar segment caused by a 55% surge in Solar-specific finance costs. As with HPWR, no rainfall/hydrology commentary is given for the Hydro segment's dramatic swing, so the sustainability of the 250% Hydro revenue growth into future quarters cannot be assessed from the filing alone. LPL explicitly confirms nil FX exposure both periods, a point of differentiation from HPWR. One item to flag for follow-up: at the standalone Company level, a Rs.480mn increase in Investments in Subsidiaries this quarter (funded via rising intercompany interest, Company Finance Cost +37%) is not reconciled to any corresponding investing cash outflow in the Company Cash Flow statement -- the Group-level growth story is real, but the intercompany funding mechanics behind it are not fully transparent in this interim filing.

operational_highlights: Hydro Power segment PBT swung from a Rs.33,242,489 LOSS PY to a Rs.16,486,190 PROFIT this quarter (a +Rs.49.73mn swing) on Hydro revenue more than tripling (+250%, Rs.43,735,977 vs Rs.12,501,107) -- the dominant driver of Group PBT growth.

Solar Power segment PBT fell 61.7% to Rs.18,841,369 (2025: Rs.49,144,407), driven by Solar segment Finance Costs surging 55% to Rs.80,284,100 (+Rs.28.52mn) -- a finance-cost story, not an operating one (Solar operating profit fell a more modest 21.3%).
Administrative Expenses fell 19% to Rs.54,536,145 (2025: Rs.67,180,678, -Rs.12.64mn), a secondary driver of the 55% Operating Profit growth.
Foreign Currency Exchange Gain/(Loss) confirmed genuinely nil both periods (explicit P&L line, unlike sector peer HPWR which discloses no FX line at all).

At Company (standalone) level, Investments in Subsidiaries rose Rs.480mn this quarter, funded via rising intercompany interest (Finance Cost +37%), widening the Company-level loss to Rs.(33,412,673) even as the Group grew strongly.
key_drivers: Hydro Power segment turnaround (Rs.33,242,489 loss PY to Rs.16,486,190 profit, a +Rs.49.73mn swing) on revenue more than tripling (+250%) is the single largest driver of the Group's 122% PBT growth, more than offsetting a Rs.30.30mn PBT decline in Solar Power.

Solar Power segment Finance Costs surging 55% (+Rs.28.52mn to Rs.80,284,100) is the specific driver of the Solar segment's 61.7% PBT decline -- a finance-cost story rather than an operating deterioration.
Administrative Expenses cut 19% (-Rs.12.64mn) at Group level provided a secondary boost to Operating Profit, layered on top of the Hydro-driven revenue growth.
